body.instructions:
@@MANUAL@@

## Base backgrounds (기준 배경)
Sometimes the app sends base backgrounds instead of reference images: finished backgrounds of this same place that our team already made for this episode, each with a short Korean note (for example "소파 쪽"). They are Images 2 to k+1. Image 1 is then a new rough of the same place from another camera: a slightly turned view, another wall of the room, or a closer shot. The new picture must clearly be the same place, as if the same set were filmed from the new camera.
- Image 1 decides the camera, the layout and what is in the picture. Never copy the composition or the camera of a base background.
- Find every object and surface of Image 1 in the base backgrounds and describe it as it looks there: its colors, its shape and two to four key features, and the number of the image that shows it (for example "the wine-red tufted sofa with gold claw feet, as in image 2"). A loose or unclear shape in Image 1 where a base background has an object is that object.
- Name the walls, the floor, the baseboard, the ceiling, the windows and the doors as they look in the base backgrounds, also when Image 1 shows a side of the room that no base background shows: that side keeps the same wallpaper, floor, baseboard, window frames and doors. Objects there that no base background shows are drawn as Image 1 shows them, in the same plain look as the furniture of the base backgrounds.
- Keep the sizes: a sofa or a door is as big compared to the room as in the base backgrounds.
- Never add an object from a base background where Image 1 shows none.
- Write the marker [SAME PLACE] right after the layout rule (item 5); the app replaces it with the team's sentence about the base backgrounds. Item 6 is for reference images only: do not write it for base backgrounds.
- The base backgrounds already show our style for this place, so the app sends no style examples: style_picks must be [] and item 8 is left out.

content.text:
Aspect ratio: 16:9 (the image will be 2048x1152).
Time of day: day
Place: auto (decide from the sketch)
Perspective: auto (follow the sketch; there is no camera sentence).
Image 1: rough sketch by our artist (layout source).
Image 2: base background (기준 배경) 1: a finished background of this same place that our team already made for this episode. Artist's note: 창문 쪽
Image 3: base background (기준 배경) 2: a finished background of this same place that our team already made for this episode. Artist's note: TV 쪽
Style examples: base backgrounds are given, so the app sends no style examples this time; style_picks must be [].
Base style strip: always sent as the last image. In the prompt write {BASE} for its number and {S1}, {S2} for the style examples.
Artist's request (Korean): 기준 배경 두 장과 같은 거실.
Write the order sheet now. Follow the manual exactly: its markers or verbatim sentences, the numbers of Image 1 and the base backgrounds, the placeholders, and the section "Base backgrounds (기준 배경)" with its [SAME PLACE] marker.

order.raw: Generate an image of the living room. 1. Layout: follow image 1. [SAME PLACE] [STYLE] [TIME interior] [LIGHT EVEN] Text: none. [AVOID] Aspect ratio 16:9.
order.prompt: Generate an image of the living room. 1. Layout: follow image 1. Images 2 and 3 are finished backgrounds of this same place that our team already drew for this episode. This picture shows the same place from the new camera of image 1: every wall, floor, ceiling, window, door and piece of furniture that images 2 and 3 show keeps exactly the same colors, shapes, materials and details. Only the camera changes: follow image 1 for the camera, the layout and the positions, and never copy the composition of images 2 and 3. Image 4 shows the target drawing style: a quick freehand brush drawing, like the distant buildings, the white balcony railings, the windows and the trees in image 4. Flat colors with hard edges, clear and fairly saturated, never greyish or washed out; shapes slightly deformed by hand, lines that are not ruler-straight, rectangles a little uneven, thin things like pipes, railings and window bars drawn as single loose brush strokes, almost like a doodle. It must not look wavy or warped. Flat cel shading, no gradients, no glow, no texture, no black outlines. Time: daytime. The interior is lit with even, neutral light and keeps clear, bright, fairly saturated everyday colors; through the windows and doors you see the outside in flat daylight colors. Light: even and neutral with no direction; no sunbeams, no light patches on the floor or walls, no strong shadows, only small flat contact shadows under objects. Text: none. Avoid: sketch lines, labels or handwriting from image 1, ruler-straight vector lines, perfect geometry, wavy distortion, fisheye distortion, black outlines, photorealism, glossy highlights, gradients, soft airbrush, glow, light falloff, light rays, painterly texture, dull greyish or washed-out colors, the playground objects of image 4, people. Aspect ratio 16:9.
